questions.question: Twenty persons take 15 days to complete a certain work. working 8 hours a day. To complete the same work in 4 days, working 10 hours a day, the number of persons required is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Twenty persons take 15 days to complete a certain work. working 8 hours a day.

Later, the same work is to be completed in 4 days, working 10 hours a day.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency of each worker × Number of Hours × Number of days to finish × Number of total workers

Calculation:

Let the efficiency of each worker be Q units a day and the number of required workers to finish the work in 4 days be N.

According to the question,

Q × 8 × 15 × 20 = Q × 10 × 4 × N

⇒ N = 60

**∴ To complete the same work in 4 days, working 10 hours a day, the number of persons required is 60.**

questions.question: After allowing a discount of 10% on the marked price of an article, it is sold for Rs. 450. Had the discount not been given, the profit would have been 25%. What is the 50% of the cost price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Marked Price (MP) = Selling Price ÷ (1 − Discount%) = 450 ÷ 0.9 = Rs. 500.

If no discount is given, SP = MP = Rs. 500, which yields a 25% profit.

Ratio of CP : MP = 100 : (100 + Profit%) = 100 : 125 = 4 : 5.

Since 5 units = Rs. 500, then 4 units (CP) = Rs. 400.

50% of CP = 400 × 0.5 = Rs. 200.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 450

Discount = 10%

Profit (without discount) = 25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a5ac90d0004d5454d77b6208786c79ec4f611f3e58d668f8480b42517c7ea53.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = SP × [100 / (100 − Discount%)]

⇒ MP = 450 × (100 / 90)

⇒ MP = 450 × (10/9) = Rs. 500

⇒ If no discount is given, New SP = MP = Rs. 500

⇒ In this case, Profit = 25%

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = New SP × [100 / (100 + Profit%)]

⇒ CP = 500 × (100 / 125)

⇒ CP = 500 × (4/5) = Rs. 400

⇒ Required value = 50% of CP = 400 × (50 / 100)

⇒ Required value = Rs. 200

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP, MP, and Profit Relationship

The relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 − Discount%).

Markup Percentage

Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100. It represents the percentage by which the cost price is increased to set the marked price.

Profit when Discount is 0

When no discount is offered, the Selling Price equals the Marked Price. Therefore, Profit = MP − CP.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the incomes of A and B is 1 ∶ 2 and that of their expenditure is 2 ∶ 3. If 80% of B's expenditure is equal to the income of A, then what is the ratio of the savings of B to the savings of A?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Income Ratio of A and B = 1 : 2

Expenditure Ratio of A and B = 2 : 3

80% of B's expenditure is equal to the income of A

Concept used:

Ratio and Proportion

Calculation:

Let the common ratio be P and Q respectively.

Hence,

The income of A and B are P and 2P respectively.

The expenditure of A and B are 2Q and 3Q respectively.

According to the question,

80% of 3Q = P

⇒ {4 over 5} × 3Q = P

⇒ P : Q = 12 : 5

Let the common ratio be k.

Thus, P = 12k and Q = 5k

Hence,

The savings of A = 12k - 2 × 5k = 2k

The savings of B = 2 × 12k - 3 × 5k = 9k

Thus, the ratio of the savings of B to the savings of A = 9k : 2k = 9 : 2

**∴ The ratio of the savings of B to the savings of A is 9 : 2.**

questions.question: 6 copies of a book can be bought for a certain sum payable at the end of a year, and 7 copies of the same book can be bought for the same sum in cash money. What is the rate per annum of simple interest (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:

6 copies of a book can be bought for a certain sum payable at the end of a year, and 7 copies of the same book can be bought for the same sum in cash money. 

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Basically, (7 - 6) = 1 book is being charged as interest on 6 books for a year if the amount is paid at the end of the year. 

Let the rate of interest be R%.

According to the question,

{(6 times R times 1) over 100} = 1

⇒ R = {100 over 6} 

⇒ R ≈ 16.7%

**∴ The rate per annum of simple interest is 16.7%.**

questions.question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is 4 m and the area of the curved surface of the cylinder is 19.5 m², then its volume (in m³) is:
questions.solution:
Given: 

The radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is 4 m

The area of the curved surface of the cylinder is 19.5 m2

Concept used:

The curved surface area of a cylinder = 2π × Radius × Height

The volume of a cylinder = π × (Radius)² × Height

Calculation:

Let the height of the cylinder be H meters.

According to the question,

2π × 4 × H = 19.5

⇒ H = {39 over 16π}

Hence, its volume = π × 4² ×{39 over 16π} = 39m³

**∴ Its volume is 39m³**.

questions.question: There are 100 students in a class, out of which 70% are girls and others are boys. The average score of girls in a test is 20% more than that of boys. If the average score of all the students is 57, then what is the average score of girls?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Total students = 100

70% are girls and the rest are boys.

The average score of girls on a test is 20% more than that of boys.

The average score of all the students is 57

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Incremented value = Initial value (1 + increase%)

Calculation:

Let the average score of the boys be Q.

Hence, the average score of the girls = 1.2Q

the total score of all boys = (100 × 30%) × Q

the total score of all girls = (100 × 70%) × (Q × 1.2)

According to the question,

(100 × 30%) × Q + (100 × 70%) × (Q × 1.2) = 100 × 57

⇒ 30Q + 84Q = 5700

⇒ Q = 50

⇒ 1.2Q = 60

**∴ The average score of girls is 60.**

questions.question: Two circles of radii 14 cm and 10 cm intersect each other. and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. What is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.solution:
Given:

PA = 10 cm

QA = 14 cm

AB = 16 cm

Concept used:

Pythagoras Theorem 

Distance between two centers divides the common chord into halves and is perpendicular to the common chord as well.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b83548b938689a429a7fcc30b940f726e06bad52f02251f60a4440b9c9a44168.png] 

AR = RB = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm

AB is perpendicular to PQ. 

Hence, PQ divides AB in halves.

Now,

PR = sqrt {10² - 8²} = 6 cm

QR = sqrt {14² - 8² } = 2√33 cm

Thus, PQ = (6 + 2√33) cm

∴ The distance between their centres is (6 + 2√33) cm.

questions.question: Which is the largest number that will divide 1992 and 233 leaving remainders 12 and 13, respectively?
questions.solution:
Given:

The largest number that will divide 1992 and 233 leaving remainders 12 and 13, respectively

Concept used:

HCF is the largest number or quantity that is a factor of each member of a group of numbers.

Calculation:

The largest number that will divide 1992 and 233 leaving remainders 12 and 13 respectively is the HCF of (1992 - 12) = 1980 and (233 - 13) = 220.

Hence, HCF (1980, 220) = 220

**∴ 220 is the largest number that will divide 1992 and 233 leaving remainders 12 and 13, respectively.**

questions.question: 'A' sells an article to 'B' at 12% profit. 'B' sells it to 'C' at 9% loss. If 'C' pays Rs. 15,288 for it, then at what price (in Rs.) is the article sold by A?
questions.solution:
Given:

'A' sells an article to 'B' at 12% profit. 'B' sells it to 'C' at 9% loss. 

'C' pays Rs. 15,288 for it.

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price (1 + Profit%)

Result of two successive percentage increment of A% and B% = (A + B + AB/100)% 

Calculation:

Final profit percentage incurred during the transaction from A to C = (12 - 9 - {12 × 9} over 100) = 1.92% (Considering 9% as negative since it's a loss)

Hence, Cost price of A = 15288 ÷ (1 + 1.92/100) = Rs. 15000

Thus, A sold the article to B at = 15000 × (1 + 12/100) = Rs. 16800

**∴ At Rs. 16800 the article is sold by A.**

questions.question: When the price of sugar gets raised by 50%, a person increases his expenditure on sugar only by 25%. By what percentage (correct up to two decimal places) should he reduce his consumption of sugar?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

New Consumption Ratio = (New Expenditure Ratio) ÷ (New Price Ratio)

Consumption Ratio = 125% ÷ 150% = 1.25 ÷ 1.50 = 5 ÷ 6

This means consumption reduces from 6 units to 5 units.

Percentage Reduction = [(6 − 5) ÷ 6] × 100 = 1 ÷ 6 × 100 = 16.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in the price of sugar = 50%

Percentage increase in expenditure = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Percentage Reduction = [(Old Consumption − New Consumption) ÷ Old Consumption] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/74aaf6297b1ef437044ddcf774256ae372cc082c93d0253a487bd5adce868a0d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of sugar be 100 and initial consumption be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = Price × Consumption = 100 × 100 = 10000

⇒ New Price = 100 + (50% of 100) = 150

⇒ New Expenditure = 10000 + (25% of 10000) = 12500

⇒ New Consumption = New Expenditure ÷ New Price

⇒ New Consumption = 12500 ÷ 150 = 250 ÷ 3 ≈ 83.33 units

⇒ Reduction in consumption = 100 − 83.33 = 16.67 units

⇒ Percentage reduction = (16.67 ÷ 100) × 100 = 16.67%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.67%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price-Consumption Relationship

If expenditure is kept constant, the ratio of old consumption to new consumption is inversely proportional to the ratio of old price to new price.

Expenditure Change Formula

Net % change in expenditure = % change in price + % change in consumption + [(% change in price × % change in consumption) ÷ 100].

Base Change Concept

If a value A is x% more than B, then B is [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100% less than A.
